posts.body_html: Here's S. leucophylla var alba (HCW clone F x MKL042) 'select clone.' It basically looks like HCW F except the white can stretch further down the petiole! Finally got a decent pitcher to snap photos of, but I think even better ones might pop in the next few weeks. posts.body_html:
Here's S. leucophylla var. alba 'Rod's Favorite,' the spring traps this time around look very washington Co, Alabama'ey. This is definitely a good candidate to experiment with in cooler climates:the entire spring overall has been abnormally cold here in the SF Bay Area, CA, and this plant is still performing well! Today, the high is 58F, with nights in the high 40's! The warmest day I can remember for the past 3 weeks was 69F! It's usually in the mid to high 70's this time of year....

Anyways, the pics! Photos taken 5/20/18. Sorry Rod, might have to re-name this to Mike's favorite LOL J/K



Unlike most leuco var. albas, this clone (so far!) colors up very easy:





Okay, the traps on these are really long and tall, maybe a bit taller than 2'. Take a look at that flower stalk, easily the tallest flower stalk I've ever seen...anywhere!

posts.body_html: To recap, S. leucophylla var. alba 'ROD's Favorite' (pictured below) dried out during a heat wave a few weeks ago, and I thought that might jack the fall traps. While it did make them smaller, the plant still pumped quite a few out! We'll see their true colors in a few weeks as the traps age and turn hopefully whiter. In the meantime, here's Rod's favorite, pic taken 9/25/18:

posts.body_html:
After a delay due to a week of crap weather in early September, Rod's favorite opened its final traps during the last heatwave of the season. These are freshly opened and will whiten further, but are already pretty dang white. Not too shabby!
